nodes.label: Plan: Close the Schedule-Quality Gap Blocking Cutover
nodes.norm_label: plan: close the schedule-quality gap blocking cutover

nodes.label: AY-to-Date Fairness Carryover
nodes.rationale: Re-measures deficit/night/weekend spread over published-snapshot history capped at 6 blocks so a resident hammered last block doesn't start even; strict no-op on empty history, and no-history residents are excluded rather than zeroed to avoid hammering the newest hire.

nodes.label: Generator Quality Harness (best-of-N + repair)
nodes.rationale: generateSchedule is greedy/nondeterministic; generateScheduleBest runs 20 seeded attempts scored via a lexicographic tuple (never a weighted scalar) plus one bounded repair pass, picking the strict best.

nodes.label: Override Capture Loop
nodes.rationale: Records every hand-edit to a generated schedule through the single updateBlockTracked choke point; reports only, never infers a rule or auto-tunes a weight, to preserve auditability.

nodes.label: SCORE_WEIGHTS Tier Audit
nodes.rationale: Every score() weight extracted into one table classified STRUCTURAL vs PREFERENCE. A real arithmetic inversion exists (preference bands up to 40 exceed the smallest structural weight of 15) but is inert because candidatePool's allAtTarget filter enforces fairness upstream; rescaling was A/B tested and rejected since it did not move deficitSpread.

nodes.label: Work-Shape Scoring
nodes.rationale: General-purpose complement to nightShapePenalty; penalizes scattered shifts, area churn, and vacation-adjacency. Fragmentation is measured against ceil(worked/maxConsecutiveWorkDays), not the night convention, because MAX_CONSECUTIVE_WORK_DAYS=6 makes multiple runs legally mandatory.

nodes.label: Quality Baseline Averaging Rework
nodes.rationale: The committed baseline was a single seed and fired on noise twice for changes that were neutral-or-better in aggregate; rebuilt as a 5-seed average plus residual per-slot tolerance, and verified it still catches a real regression.

nodes.label: Codex Review Blocked (Usage Quota)
nodes.rationale: Three codex exec invocations all died on an ERROR: usage limit before producing output; per skill rules the failure is surfaced rather than a verdict fabricated. Plan shipped locked by Act 1 but unreviewed by Act 2.

nodes.label: Phase 0 Measured Result: Rescale Rejected
nodes.rationale: Weight inversion confirmed real (up to 8 shifts of deficit overridable by an area nudge, preexisting comment was false) but rescaling preferences ~6x down did not move deficitSpread over 6 seeds x 3 fixtures and slightly worsened coverageMiss, because candidatePool's allAtTarget filter already enforces fairness upstream of score().

nodes.label: Track A: Shared-Password Admin Gating
nodes.community_name: User Feedback + Admin Portal Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: This app has no auth system of its own (whoever has the URL/env vars has full read-write to res_state), so a shared server-checked password is the only viable admin gate — matches the same pattern used by sibling Kitchen Inventory and ecowater-pricing-app.

nodes.label: PWA HTML Shell
nodes.rationale: Injects Vite %VITE_*% tokens into window.__SUPABASE_URL__/__SUPABASE_ANON__/__ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAIN__ rather than import.meta.env directly, so a build with no .env leaves a literal unresolved token the app treats as 'not configured'.

nodes.label: Apple Touch Icon
nodes.rationale: Solid theme-color placeholder square referenced by index.html's apple-touch-icon link tag for iOS home-screen installs.

nodes.label: 192px App Icon
nodes.rationale: Solid theme-color placeholder square matching icon-512 at a smaller PWA manifest size.

nodes.label: 512px App Icon
nodes.rationale: Solid theme-color (#0057B8) placeholder square, no logo mark or text — PWA manifest icon, not a designed brand asset.

nodes.label: Cloud Sync (Supabase)
nodes.rationale: Optional cross-device sync via hand-rolled fetch-based PostgREST client, gated by SUPABASE_ENABLED; last-write-wins, dbReady gates all cloud writes so a device that never read cloud can't overwrite newer data.

nodes.label: Demo Sandbox
nodes.rationale: Lets an admin practice on a disposable copy of the whole workspace, isolated by physical localStorage key prefix (physKey) rather than a mode flag inside shared code.

nodes.label: Circadian Scheduling Rules
nodes.rationale: Hard checks run in validateAll regardless of appSettings.enforceRest; that toggle only ever gated the pairwise legal-rest-hours check, matching the generator which already enforced circadian rules unconditionally.

nodes.label: Chief-Editable Journal Club Dates
nodes.rationale: Journal Club defaults to first Tuesdays but the chief occasionally moves one, so the date list is now stored data with an explicit empty array honored as 'no JC this year'.

nodes.label: Journal Club Rules
nodes.rationale: Worked-JC derived from SHIFT_TIMING overlap with 18:00-21:00, not a hand-maintained shift-id list, so it automatically covers PED-S and Trauma Night; capped at 3/AY counted only across published blocks.

nodes.label: PED-N Split Into Two Shift IDs
nodes.norm_label: ped-n split into two shift ids
nodes.rationale: One PED-N used to model two different real-world shifts at the wrong hours for one of them; split into PED-N (EM residents, 19:00-04:00) and PED-N-FM (FM-3 only, 23:00-08:00), which made night-to-evening-next-day legal for the first time and required widening the postNightRest circadian scan.

nodes.label: Accessibility Floor
nodes.rationale: Visible keyboard focus, WCAG-AA contrast on tinted status blocks, labeled form fields, aria-labels on icon-only buttons — non-negotiable baseline given the field-use context.

nodes.label: Field-Ready Design System
nodes.rationale: Synced (not authored) from the sibling ems-inventory project so this app visually reads as one family with OMD Response and other UTHealth EM tools; must read instantly in sunlight or a dark cab, so the rule is 'quiet, chunky, high-contrast, utilitarian' with one bold element per screen.

nodes.label: Semantic Palette Tokens & Dark-Mode Constraint
nodes.rationale: Dark mode works by remapping a hard-coded list of literal Tailwind utilities in src/index.css; introducing a new literal palette family (zinc/slate/stone/etc.) would silently render light-mode colors in dark mode, so only 8 allowed families plus semantic tokens may be used.

nodes.label: Typography System (Barlow / Barlow Condensed / JetBrains Mono)
nodes.norm_label: typography system (barlow / barlow condensed / jetbrains mono)
nodes.rationale: font-mono reserved for all data readouts (counts, coverage, dates, shift times) so numeric fields read unambiguously at a glance; font-display reserved for titles/stats to keep hierarchy legible under field conditions.

nodes.label: Pre-authorization Email Allowlist
nodes.rationale: Allowlisted address lands in admin role on first login instead of pending; keyed off auth.jwt() email never client-controlled new.email, so nobody can spoof an allowlisted address.

nodes.label: Server-side Domain Restriction
nodes.rationale: Client-side LoginScreen check alone is insufficient; restrict_signup_domain SQL hook wired to a Before-User-Created Auth Hook enforces it server-side.

nodes.label: RLS as Security Boundary
nodes.rationale: UI gates are convenience only; RLS is the real boundary. role='pending' must be enforced in RLS policies, not just the client branch, after a real impersonation hole was found.

nodes.label: Coverage Min/Max Model
nodes.rationale: Generator fills every shift to min first (hard), then optionally tops up toward max only for residents under their own target (soft cap, never a requirement).

nodes.label: FLEX/POD Seniority Composition
nodes.rationale: FLEX seniority stays soft (chief's call); POD seniority is hard-errored in validateAll unless a Wellness-Wednesday PGY-2 substitute applies. Wednesday day shifts are exempt from both rules since Grand Rounds structurally removes every EM senior that day.

nodes.label: 12-Hour Shift Windows
nodes.rationale: Backward compat is the whole design: absent twelveHourWindows falls back to implicit conference windows reproducing the old hardcoded swap exactly, so an untouched AY behaves identically to before the feature.

nodes.label: Wellness Wednesdays
nodes.rationale: Block-relative Nth Wednesday (not calendar month) per EM_HOME resident; every getEligibleShifts call site must pass ctx.blockStart or this silently no-ops.

nodes.label: Chief Roles
nodes.rationale: Global roster field replacing the old per-block isChief checkbox; only the academic role carries a hard rule (no Tuesday eve/night).

nodes.label: Jeopardy & Sick-Call Ledger
nodes.rationale: One incident record per event with sick-call and activation counts derived from it so they can never disagree; nothing auto-applies to any target, same restraint as override capture.

nodes.label: Per-Block Target Overrides (Buy-Downs)
nodes.rationale: A delta, never an absolute number, so it survives SHIFT_TARGETS changes; a delta that zeroes the target must return null not 0, since 0 != null is true and would corrupt fairness scoring.

nodes.label: Eligibility Overrides as Diff
nodes.rationale: Used to store a wholesale snapshot of the shift list, meaning a shift id added later was invisible to that override forever; a real outage happened when 12h replacement shifts could never be assigned because saved rotation overrides predated those ids. A diff has no such blind spot.

nodes.label: Rule-Default Migration (LEGACY_*_DEFAULTS)
nodes.rationale: getEffectiveDayRules replaces a key's default wholesale with any chief-saved override, so a saved override equal to the previous (pre-correction) default would silently keep masking a fix forever without this pruning mechanism.

nodes.label: Caveman Terse-Response Mode (Cline rule)
nodes.rationale: Forces terse, fragment-style responses to cut filler/fluff and save tokens while keeping technical substance and code exact; auto-suspends for security warnings, irreversible actions, or user confusion, and never applies to code/commits/PRs.

nodes.label: Caveman Terse-Response Mode (Copilot rule)
nodes.rationale: Same terse-response contract as the Cline/Windsurf/OpenCode/AGENTS variants, ported to GitHub Copilot's own instructions file so the behavior is consistent across every AI tool configured for this repo.

nodes.label: Caveman Terse-Response Mode (OpenCode rule)
nodes.rationale: Same terse-response contract ported to OpenCode's AGENTS.md convention.

nodes.label: Caveman Terse-Response Mode (Windsurf rule)
nodes.rationale: Same terse-response contract for Windsurf, marked with 'trigger: always_on' frontmatter so it applies to every session without manual activation.

nodes.label: Caveman Terse-Response Mode (top-level AGENTS.md)
nodes.rationale: Same terse-response contract as the tool-specific variants, placed at repo root as the generic AGENTS.md convention.

nodes.label: Dark Mode
nodes.rationale: Override stylesheet in index.css rather than Tailwind dark: variants, since the file has thousands of class strings.

nodes.label: PDF Export (jspdf-autotable)
nodes.rationale: jspdf-autotable@3.8.4's default export is not callable under esbuild/Rollup bundling; fixed by importing for side effect only and always calling doc.autoTable(...) as an instance method.

nodes.label: QGenda CSV Export Rework
nodes.rationale: Chief has no QGenda admin rights and cannot trial-run, so every choice (task-name table, column-name data, per-resident staffId escape hatch) is biased toward being chief-fixable without a redeploy.

nodes.label: Soft Rule Priority
nodes.rationale: Chief-orderable ranking of coverageMin, seniorComposition, postNightRest decides whether the generator reaches for a rest-violating/junior candidate or leaves a slot unfilled to protect a rule.

nodes.label: What's New Banner
nodes.rationale: Shown once automatically because deploys are otherwise invisible to the chief; a prior UI change shipped unnoticed.

nodes.rationale: Approval writes straight into the resident's existing approvedDatesOff array, the exact field getEligibleShifts/the generator/the grid already treat as a hard block — so no changes to the eligibility/generator engine are needed.

nodes.label: Task 12: Email Notifications (Resend Edge Function)
nodes.rationale: Fails soft — a Resend error is logged, not thrown, so a flaky email provider never blocks the underlying database write that triggered the webhook (fired after the write already committed).

nodes.norm_label: task 1: supabase auth client + config plumbing

nodes.label: Task 2: profiles + day_off_requests Schema & RLS
nodes.rationale: BEFORE UPDATE triggers (enforce_resident_id_immutable, enforce_cancel_only_status) close gaps plain RLS WITH CHECK can't express, e.g. WITH CHECK alone can't guarantee 'no other column changed' during a cancel, and IS DISTINCT FROM (not =/!=) is required so NULL columns don't defeat the guard.

nodes.label: Task 3: Server-Side Email-Domain Signup Restriction
nodes.rationale: A client-side-only domain check is trivially bypassed by calling Supabase's auth REST API directly with the public anon key (visible in this public repo's deployed bundle regardless), so enforcement must live in a Postgres 'Before User Created' Auth Hook.

nodes.norm_label: task 8: resident's own request list + cancel

nodes.label: Task 9: Chief-Side Requests Tab (Login/Role Gate)
nodes.rationale: ApprovalQueue is deliberately a separate component, not inlined into RequestsTab's conditional-return body, because placing its hooks after early returns that fire conditionally across renders would violate the Rules of Hooks.

nodes.label: Known Limitation: 'Residents Never See Schedule' is UI-only
nodes.norm_label: known limitation: 'residents never see schedule' is ui-only
nodes.rationale: Consciously accepted, not a bug: /requests reads the same wide-open-RLS res_state row as the chief's cloud sync, so the entire schedule crosses the wire before the UI narrows it; the unauthenticated '/' route can also be visited directly. Closing this for real would need a narrow RLS-scoped view/Edge Function plus real auth on '/' — out of scope for this feature.

nodes.label: RLS Policy Design (resident vs chief scoping)
nodes.norm_label: rls policy design (resident vs chief scoping)
nodes.rationale: Residents may only INSERT/SELECT their own resident_id rows and UPDATE status pending->cancelled; only a chief profile may SELECT all / decide any row — this is the app's first real per-user RLS, distinct from res_state's wide-open posture.
